findings.description:
Authorization check uses logical AND instead of logical OR when checking if the user is a team admin or owner. — WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed using logical `&&` instead of `||` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`.
WHY: Team admins and team owners are distinct membership roles; using `&&` prevents team admins and team owners from adding guests to team bookings unless they somehow satisfy both checks simultaneously.
HOW: Replace `&&` with `||` so that either team admins or team owners are permitted.

Failed device tagging leaves the device cached in localCache, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests. — WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` sets the device key in `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` completes, leaving the entry cached when `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (or any DB error) occurs.
WHY: When a new device is rejected because the device limit is reached, subsequent requests with the same device ID hit `localCache.Get(key)` and return `nil`, bypassing authentication rejection and defeating the device limit.
HOW: Update `tagDeviceUI` to only store the key in `localCache` after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or explicitly remove the key from `localCache` if `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error.

recordLegacyDuration is mistakenly called instead of recordStorageDuration when Storage.Create fails. — WHAT: `recordLegacyDuration` is called when `d.Storage.Create` returns an error.
WHY: Storage failure metrics are recorded into legacy storage metrics instead of unified storage metrics, skewing operational metrics and alerting.
HOW: Change `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` to `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.

recordLegacyDuration is mistakenly called instead of recordStorageDuration when Storage.Update fails. — WHAT: `recordLegacyDuration` is called when `d.Storage.Update` fails.
WHY: Unified storage update errors are incorrectly recorded under legacy duration metrics.
HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.

recordStorageDuration is mistakenly called instead of recordLegacyDuration for asynchronous legacy DeleteCollection. — WHAT: `recordStorageDuration` is called inside the legacy delete collection goroutine instead of `recordLegacyDuration`.
WHY: Legacy collection deletion metrics are erroneously attributed to the primary unified storage metric counters.
HOW: Call `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`.

Object name is passed as kind label to recordStorageDuration on successful Delete. — WHAT: `name` is passed as the `kind` parameter in `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`.
WHY: It populates Prometheus metrics with high-cardinality object names instead of the resource kind, inflating metric series cardinality and corrupting per-kind duration tracking.
HOW: Pass `options.Kind` instead of `name`.

Record storage duration instead of legacy duration when unified storage Create fails. — WHAT: `recordLegacyDuration` is called when `d.Storage.Create` returns an error.
WHY: Failures when creating objects in unified storage are misattributed to legacy storage metrics instead of unified storage metrics.
HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`.

Pass options.Kind instead of name to recordStorageDuration in Delete. — WHAT: `name` is passed as the `kind` parameter in `recordStorageDuration` for Delete.
WHY: Sets the Prometheus metric `kind` label to the object's instance name rather than its resource kind, corrupting metric dimensions and causing high cardinality.
HOW: Pass `options.Kind` instead of `name` to `d.recordStorageDuration`.

Record storage duration instead of legacy duration when unified storage Update fails. — WHAT: `recordLegacyDuration` is called when `d.Storage.Update` fails.
WHY: Unified storage update errors are incorrectly recorded under legacy storage duration metrics.
HOW: Call `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead.

Record legacy duration instead of storage duration when deleting collections from legacy storage. — WHAT: `recordStorageDuration` is called inside the legacy delete collection goroutine instead of `recordLegacyDuration`.
WHY: Asynchronous legacy delete collection durations and error statuses are recorded into storage metrics instead of legacy metrics.
HOW: Change `d.recordStorageDuration` to `d.recordLegacyDuration` inside the goroutine.

Feed polling crashes when RSS feed items use `<description>` or lack `<content>` because `i.content` is nil. — WHAT: `i.content.scrub` is called on `SimpleRSS` items without checking if `i.content` is nil or falling back to `i.description`.
WHY: Standard RSS 2.0 feeds without `<content>` tags return `nil` for `i.content`, causing a `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` that crashes the entire `PollFeed` job.
HOW: Fall back to `i.description` (or empty string) and guard against nil before calling `.scrub`.

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` without requiring `open-uri`. — WHAT: `open(url)` is invoked in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` without ensuring `open-uri` is required.
WHY: When `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is executed in a context where `open-uri` has not been loaded (e.g., via `RetrieveTopic` background job when feed polling is disabled), Ruby's default `Kernel#open` will treat the HTTP URL as a local file path and raise `Errno::ENOENT`.
HOW: Add `require 'open-uri'` at the top of `app/models/topic_embed.rb` or within `import_remote`.

Missing type="button" on 'Lost access' and 'Cancel' buttons causes unwanted form submission in DisableTwoFactorModal. — WHAT: The 'Lost access' and 'Cancel' buttons inside `<Form form={form} handleSubmit={handleDisable}>` lack `type="button"` and do not call `e.preventDefault()`.
WHY: In HTML forms, buttons default to `type="submit"`, so clicking 'Lost access' or 'Cancel' triggers form validation and submission via `handleDisable` instead of simply switching the view or canceling.
HOW: Add `type="button"` to the 'Lost access' and 'Cancel' `<Button>` elements.

Add explicit type="button" to the 'lost_access' button to prevent triggering form submission. — WHAT: The 'lost access' toggle button inside `<Form>` lacks `type="button"`.
WHY: Buttons inside a `<form>` element default to `type="submit"`, which causes clicking 'lost access' / 'go back' to trigger form submission (`handleDisable`) and validation errors instead of simply toggling the input mode.
HOW: Add `type="button"` to the `<Button>` component so clicking it does not submit the form.

Use default_factory for dataclass timestamp default instead of evaluating timezone.now() at module load time. — WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported rather than dynamically when an `AssignmentSource` instance is created.
WHY: Every `AssignmentSource` instance initialized without an explicit `queued` value will share the same stale timestamp from module load time, producing incorrect timestamps when tracking when assignments were queued.
HOW: Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` from the `dataclasses` module to evaluate `timezone.now()` upon each instantiation.

Duplicate `self.downsize` method definition overwrites the 4/5-argument overload and breaks callers passing width and height. — WHAT: Duplicate `def self.downsize` definition overwrites the 4/5-argument overload (`from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}`).
WHY: In Ruby, defining a method with the same name replaces the prior definition; callers passing width and height as separate arguments (such as `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) will fail at runtime with an `ArgumentError` or corrupted options.
HOW: Consolidate `self.downsize` into a single method that checks argument types to handle both dimension strings and `max_width`/`max_height` arguments.

Guard against nil host in before_validation and downcase host in SQL query. — WHAT: `before_validation` calls `sub!` on `self.host` without guarding against `nil`, and `record_for_host` queries `lower(host) = ?` without downcasing the input host parameter. WHY: Validating a record with a nil host crashes with `NoMethodError` instead of producing model validation errors, and URLs containing uppercase hostnames fail the database lookup due to case sensitivity. HOW: Add a `self.host.present?` guard in `before_validation` and pass `host.downcase` to `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

Use lazy modelSupplier with null guard in getSubGroupsCount to prevent NullPointerException during concurrent access. — Replace direct invocation of getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount() with lazy modelSupplier.get() and add a null guard to prevent NullPointerException when a cached group's backing model is deleted or missing during concurrent access.
